cards.text: Amos, one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, has been bringing the LORD's word to Israel (Amos 1:1). Now he calls out to some women living on Mount Samaria, and he opens with, "Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Mount Samaria." Friend, if somebody opened a conversation with ME like that, I'd climb right back into the junk drawer.

cards.question: Amos says these women on Mount Samaria oppress the poor and crush the ___.

cards.text: And they tell their husbands, "Bring us more to drink." Then the Lord GOD swears an oath, and He swears it by His holiness.

cards.question: The Lord GOD swears by His holiness about these women of Samaria. What does He say is coming for them?

answers.text: They will be taken away with hooks
They will be crowned in Samaria
They will be given more land

cards.text: Hooks for them, and fishhooks for their posterity. Friend, I've been pulled out of a drawer before, and trust me, THAT was the gentle kind of pulling.

cards.question: When these women are taken away, the LORD says they will walk out through the city's strong, unbroken walls.

cards.text: Out through broken walls, each one straight ahead of her, cast out toward Harmon. Then the LORD turns to Israel's worship, and friend, listen close, because this is going to sound backwards.

cards.question: The LORD sends Israel to Bethel and to Gilgal. What does He say they'll do there?

answers.text: Repent and turn back to Him

cards.text: And He keeps going: "Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days." EVERY THREE DAYS, friend, and I can't even remember to dust my gold base that often.

cards.question: Along with leavened bread as a thank offering, the LORD tells Israel to keep their freewill offerings quiet.
All those sacrifices, tithes and loud offerings. Why does the LORD say the children of Israel keep it all going?

answers.text: It's what they love to do

cards.text: Now the LORD lists what He already sent Israel's way. First, He afflicted all their cities with cleanness of teeth and all their towns with lack of bread.

cards.question: Even with lack of bread in all their towns, Israel still did not ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: Keep your ears on that line, yet you did not return to Me, because it keeps coming back. Next, the LORD held back the rain when the harvest was three months away.

cards.question: When the LORD held back the rain from Israel, He held it back from every city and every field alike.

cards.text: One field got rain, and another withered without it. People staggered from city to city for water to drink, and they still weren't satisfied.
And there it is again: yet you did not return to Me. So the LORD struck their growing gardens and vineyards with blight and mildew.

cards.question: Blight and mildew hit Israel's gardens and vineyards. What devoured their fig and olive trees?

cards.text: Same ending: yet you did not return to Me. Then the LORD sent plagues among them like those of Egypt, and He killed their young men with the sword, along with their captured horses.

cards.question: Plagues and the sword came on Israel. What does the LORD say He filled their nostrils with?

cards.text: And still, yet you did not return to Me. Then the LORD brings up two cities from way back in Genesis.

cards.question: The LORD says He overthrew some of Israel the same way He overthrew which two cities?
The LORD says the ones who were left were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze. What does that picture show?

cards.text: Five times now: yet you did not return to Me, and friend, when MY oven timer goes off five times, even I come running. Eventually.

cards.question: The LORD says that is what He will do to Israel. Then what does He tell Israel to do?

cards.text: Then the words turn to who this God is. He forms the mountains, and He creates the wind.

cards.question: The God who forms the mountains and creates the wind keeps His thoughts hidden from people.
The One who forms the mountains and creates the wind has a name. What is it?

answers.text: The LORD the God of Hosts

cards.text: He turns the dawn to darkness and strides on the heights of the earth. And THAT, friend, is the God on the other side of "prepare to meet your God."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Mount Samaria.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 18 quotes "prepare to meet your God.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin was 'pulled out of a drawer.' His backstory says the angel called him out and the drawer was simply gone. He was never pulled out, so the joke adds something new to his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The setup says 'this is going to sound backwards' just before card 8 asks what Israel will do at Bethel and Gilgal. That hint rules out 'Repent and turn back to Him' and 'Rest and celebrate together,' which gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'So the LORD struck their growing gardens' makes the blight a result of Israel not returning. Amos 4:9 only lists it as the next thing the LORD sent. It never says how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says Sodom and Gomorrah are 'from way back in Genesis' but gives no reference for that fact, which comes from outside the passage (Genesis 19:24-25).

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The question calls the firebrand group 'the ones who were left.' Amos 4:11 only says 'you were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze.' It doesn't say which group 'you' is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'Five times now' counts the refrain across Amos 4:6-11, but the card cites only Amos 4:11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Run back to Bethel' can be argued right. In Amos 4:4 the LORD tells Israel, 'Go to Bethel and transgress.'

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Most story cards in this stop (1, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 15) are flat retellings with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line. In 18 cards, only card 13 sounds like Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
